name: Guardian Standard of Recovery heals the amount its buff advertises, including Strength scaling (#6604)
contract: Standard of Recovery 500260 summons creature 50053, which casts 500266 on itself: an APPLY_AREA_AURA_FRIEND whose effect 0 is aura 23 SPELL_AURA_PERIODIC_TRIGGER_SPELL with EffectBasePoints 79 (amount 80) and Amplitude 3000, triggering the direct heal 500248. The buff's own aura tooltip (Spell.dbc column 187) is the client-visible contract and reads 'A nearby Standard of Recovery is causing you to regenerate ${$w1+$STR*.25} health every $t1 sec', i.e. the aura's own effect amount plus 0.25 x the owner's Strength. Effect 1 is the '+$s2% healing received' half, aura 319 with BasePoints 5. The tick is script-driven: aura_ascension_guardian_recovery::Tick prevents the native trigger and re-casts 500248 with an explicit amount. The bug (#6604, level 30, core 4666cd9941c0) is that the script built that amount from the triggered spell 500248's own EffectBasePoints (79 -> base 2), not from the standard aura's effect amount (80): at the reporter's 124 Strength the buff advertised 80 + 31 = 111 health but the tick healed 2 + 31 = 33. This scenario pins the contract at level 1, where the Strength term is at most a few points, so the ratio of one tick's effective healing to the aura's own advertised amount is 1 for a correct tick and ~0.03 for the defect. The heal target's health is fixtured low with a large pool so nothing is overhealed.

steps.label: SETUP: the starter Hearthstone satisfies 500260's TotemCategory 5
The Standard of Recovery banner summons
The owner carries the Standard's periodic buff
CONTRACT: the buff's advertised amount $w1 is the Standard aura's own 80
SETUP: a level-one owner's Strength keeps the 0.25 x Strength term small
Fixture a low health inside a large pool so the tick is never overhealed
One tick heals the buff's advertised amount plus the Strength term (fails while the tick heals 500248's own base)
The heal lands through the native heal log
